verdict.summary: Issue #213 at verified version aada29af45e1bb5a6c3a3e61f95af32d86d0c7ba428dfc4c9bd3291524f6c69e is blocked. Its architecture and provider assumptions are stale, acceptance can succeed vacuously, ownership overlaps active runtime issues, and failure, evidence, and rollout contracts are incomplete.

blockingFindings.title: Dispatch design conflicts with the canonical Agent OS authority boundary
blockingFindings.details: The issue assigns provider-specific OAuth adapters, credential-home use, route enabling, and local fallback to an unspecified gateway or library. Trusted policy requires every model-backed turn, credential interaction, concrete execution decision, and route provenance to remain exclusively behind the canonical Agent OS launcher, with no repository-local fallback. Rewrite the scope to identify the runtime-owned integration boundary and prohibit direct provider execution or credential handling outside it.

blockingFindings.title: The provider baseline is stale and presently unverifiable
blockingFindings.details: The issue claims that all four registry entries are disabled, that Kimi is an unproven LiteLLM path, and that Claude, Codex, and Agy require new custom adapters. Verified state instead records canonical routes for all four providers, Kimi as decommissioned, Codex as quota-blocked until 2026-07-23, and Agy's receipts lane as credential_missing under issue #293. The contract must be refreshed against current route configuration and state before implementation can be selected or live proofs required.

blockingFindings.title: Requirements and acceptance permit a vacuous or deferred result
blockingFindings.details: “Implement or explicitly scope” permits documentation without delivery, while “each enabled provider has a live proof” can pass with no providers enabled. The issue does not state the required terminal state for Claude, Codex, Agy, or Kimi. Define an objective per-provider outcome—enabled with named proof criteria, or intentionally disabled for a named blocking condition—and make completion require every listed outcome.

blockingFindings.title: Single-lane ownership and dependency ordering are unresolved
blockingFindings.details: The issue spans four provider integrations, shared credential and routing behavior, live operations, and local degradation without identifying one implementation lane or sequencing dependencies. Its scope potentially overlaps gateway issues #210, #211, and #214 and active runtime work in #253, #275, #291, and #293. Establish explicit dependency links, define which issue owns route resolution, credential repair, provider recovery, and gateway integration, and remove duplicated acceptance.

blockingFindings.title: Failure and never-meter behavior are not defined precisely
blockingFindings.details: The issue names quota exhaustion and generic fail-closed behavior but does not define outcomes for missing, expired, or revoked credentials; refresh failure; timeout; malformed responses; route unavailability; or ambiguous quota classification. “Safe never-meter behavior” is undefined, and the requested local fallback conflicts with the prohibition on repository-local execution fallback. Specify runtime-owned error classes, allowed transitions, metered-route exclusion rules, and fail-closed behavior for every failure class.

blockingFindings.title: Validation and live-proof evidence are not reproducible
blockingFindings.details: “Live proof on record” does not identify the receipt schema, immutable revision, provider and adapter version, route provenance, credential gate, expected observations, freshness, storage location, or redaction checks. Mock coverage is also described only by topic. Define authoritative test commands and cases, the exact credential-gated proof procedure, required normalized evidence fields, secret-leak assertions, and the checks that distinguish unavailable, quota-blocked, disabled, and healthy routes.

blockingFindings.title: Enablement rollout and rollback are unspecified
blockingFindings.details: The issue allows providers to be enabled after proof but defines no configuration owner, staged rollout, proof-expiry policy, health observation window, kill switch, rollback trigger, or behavior when a previously proven provider loses credentials or quota. Add per-provider admission and rollback procedures governed by canonical route status, including how evidence is published without exposing secrets.

nonBlockingNotes: Owner decision required: should #213 be rewritten as an Agent OS runtime-mediated cloud-dispatch contract, explicitly reconciling Kimi's decommissioned state and Agy's #293 credential gate, or retired in favor of the active route and receipt issues #253, #275, #291, and #293?

verdict.summary: Final independent review of marius-patrik/Andromeda issue #213 at verified version 5b624a729d68571cfd6b808401a5870ffdd3898aa2a26adc1156b7c98246d62f found four blocking contract gaps involving receipt ownership, rollout determinism, evidence publication, and submodule validation.

blockingFindings.title: Admission receipt requirements conflict with dependency ownership
blockingFindings.details: Issue #213 says #275 exclusively owns the required verified receipt contract, but the supplied #275 contract defines an exact schema that lacks #213's credential-gate, billing-class, adapter, route-transition, observation, validation, and secret-scan fields. The specification does not state whether #275 must be changed or whether #213 owns a separate versioned admission record referencing the immutable #275 receipt. Implementation would therefore either duplicate another lane or be unable to satisfy #213 acceptance.

blockingFindings.title: Promotion and rollback criteria are not deterministically observable
blockingFindings.details: Promotion requires a 24-hour observation window with no listed failures, but the contract does not define the observation source, required traffic or probes, window boundaries, evaluator, or whether an idle window can pass. Rollback on a repeated malformed response or timeout likewise has no count, time window, or reset rule. These omissions prevent objective testing and consistent route-state transitions.

blockingFindings.title: Canonical evidence destination and schema are unverifiable
blockingFindings.details: The issue requires a schema-valid receipt in a Git-backed canonical evidence store and a marker-owned public comment, but identifies neither the repository and path nor an authoritative schema or marker format. A field list alone does not establish serialization, required-value constraints, canonical digest calculation, update identity, or validation ownership, so the publication and freshness acceptance criteria cannot be reproduced against an exact evidence reference.

blockingFindings.title: Submodule pointer validation does not satisfy the repository overlay
blockingFindings.details: The implementation lane targets canonical Agent OS runtime surfaces in a submodule-root repository, yet the contract neither forbids gitlink changes nor defines their admissible paths. The required recursive submodule-status command detects only part of the pointer state and does not prove child identity, configured URL, released default-branch ancestry, accessibility, or green required evidence. The issue must either exclude gitlink updates explicitly or require the complete trusted pointer contract for every changed gitlink.

nonBlockingNotes: Owner decision required: choose whether #275 is amended to own the expanded admission-receipt schema or #213 owns a separately versioned record that references #275's immutable execution receipt.
Owner decision required: define the authoritative observation source and idle-window policy, plus the malformed-response and timeout rollback threshold and reset window.
Owner decision required: designate the canonical evidence repository/path and the authoritative receipt and public-marker schemas.

verdict.summary: Issue #213 has clear ownership, dependencies, trust boundaries, validation commands, evidence publication, and staged rollout, but two contract ambiguities prevent deterministic implementation and validation.

blockingFindings.title: Route states and normalized outcomes lack one exhaustive state machine
blockingFindings.details: The contract alternates between `disabled` as a route status and phrases such as "disabled as quota_blocked", "disabled as credential_missing", and "disabled as decommissioned", while the schema status enumeration treats those reason codes as distinct statuses. No separate enabled flag or reason field is required. Rollback likewise selects an unspecified "disabled or blocked status", and no normalized successful-proof outcome is defined. Specify exhaustive status and outcome enums plus the exact before/after transition for every admission, failure, rollback, and required provider terminal state.

blockingFindings.title: Observation evidence does not fully define the data needed to reproduce promotion and rollback
blockingFindings.details: Promotion compares route-configuration and credential-state digests, while rollback depends on an immutable route tuple, checkpoint series, and counter resets. These fields and their representations are not explicitly required by the admission-record field list or authoritative schema contract. The credential-state digest derivation is also undefined, so implementations could expose a credential-derived hash, change identity on refresh, or produce incompatible values. Require schema fields for the complete immutable tuple, series/checkpoint identity, T0, counter inputs and resets, and define a canonical non-secret credential-state attestation produced by the credential owner.

verdict.summary: Issue #213 version 483f3184ca7b184e70a865b43331c08c4651b690c3dce29be9cffe8fedc0fdbc remains blocked by six internal contract gaps affecting admission, deterministic outcomes, evidence, and validation.

blockingFindings.title: Disabled routes have no valid path into admission probing
blockingFindings.details: The contract says routes begin disabled, disabled routes must be rejected before dispatch with their persistent reason, and enabled is true only for probing or healthy. It simultaneously requires a first live proof to transition a disabled route to probing and requires fresh recovery proofs for Codex and Agy. No eligible-but-disabled state, admission-probe exception, or pre-proof transition exists, so initial admission and recovery cannot occur without violating the state machine. Define the exact runtime-owned transition that permits a credential-gated proof while retaining fail-closed rejection for administrative and decommissioned routes.

blockingFindings.title: Concurrent gate failures lack deterministic precedence
blockingFindings.details: Administrative state, proof expiry, credential state, quota state, billing eligibility, route availability, and receipt validation can overlap, but the contract does not define which normalized outcome and transition wins. This is material because the required Kimi, Agy, and Codex terminal outcomes depend on specific classifications even when other gates also fail. Specify a complete gate evaluation order and precedence matrix, including which checks may access credential metadata or perform network dispatch.

blockingFindings.title: No command deterministically produces required disabled-route evidence
blockingFindings.details: Acceptance requires evidence records for Codex, Agy, and Kimi in their disabled terminal states, including a non-dispatched Kimi record. The live command is specified to prove only currently eligible configured routes, while the observation command handles probing routes and the evidence command only validates existing records. Therefore ineligible routes can be omitted with no authoritative producer for their required records. Define a provider-agnostic command behavior that enumerates all required routes and emits schema-valid pre-dispatch records without invoking ineligible providers.

blockingFindings.title: The claimed exhaustive transition model has unmapped values
blockingFindings.details: A route disabled by the rollback kill switch has reason repeated_malformed_timeout, and later pre-dispatch rejection must use an outcome matching its persistent reason, but repeated_malformed_timeout is absent from normalizedOutcome. In addition, keep_terminal_state is an allowed transitionAction with no event or invariant defining when it is required. Complete the outcome and transition mapping so every reachable persistent state has exactly one valid subsequent record representation.

blockingFindings.title: Secret-leak failures cannot satisfy the mandatory evidence schema
blockingFindings.details: The state machine requires secret_leak_detected records and transitions, while every record unconditionally requires secretScan.status to equal passed for scans covering arguments, logs, errors, receipts, and published evidence. A scan that detects a leak cannot truthfully pass, leaving the required failure unrecordable as schema-valid evidence. Separate detection from sanitized-publication validation or add an explicit failed/detected representation with fail-closed publication rules.

blockingFindings.title: Immutable execution-receipt storage and reference provenance are undefined
blockingFindings.details: Issue #275 creates its receipt as a new file inside the caller worktree, while #213 stores admission evidence in Andromeda-data and requires validators to reject references outside that evidence repository. The contract does not define where the immutable #275 receipt is committed, how its bytes are transferred without forking or reinterpreting its schema, or which repository and revision the receipt reference identifies. Define the authoritative receipt destination and byte-preserving publication/reference procedure before executed admissions can be validated.

nonBlockingNotes: The dependencies on #253, #275, #293, and #291 are explicitly assigned and remain subject to refreshed live-state verification before implementation or enablement.
